newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shrs end at new record on economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shrs end at new record on economic reforms.

text.p: Prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange surged to a fifth consecutive record high in heavy trade on bullish sentiment over Venezuela's economic reforms fueled by foreign buyers, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index rose 2.54 percent to 8,395.77.
Market leader Electricidad de Caracas, which routinely accounts for over half of total trade, led the rally, jumping 27.50 bolivars to 649.00 bolivars.
With demand for shares still strong at close of trade, brokers said the rally could continue for several days.
"It looks like we could continue seeing rises because the market in general is in highly demand," said Mario Simosa of the Multinvest brokerage.

The opening up of Venezuela's oil industry and key labor law reforms in recent weeks continue to be the main catalysts for the market's performance with foreign investment funds taking an increasing strong interest in Venezuelan stocks, brokers said.
"There's great euphoria, a lot of foreign funds entering," said Roberto Isasi, an analyst with Merinvest.
A total of 30 stocks rose, 12 fell and two remained flat in trade of 21.352 billion bolivars ($44.1 million).

Among other big gainers were telephone company CANTV, which rose 185 bolivars to 2,925.00 bolivars, cement company Vencemos, whose class 1 stock rose 65.00 bolivars to 635.00 bolivars and class 2 stock rose 38.00 bolivars to 510.00 bolivars.
The composite Merinvest index, which includes CANTV, rose 3.76 percent to 132.63.
